text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for an end to the present Middle East crisis, praising Egyptian and international efforts and hoping for fruitful results from U.S. initiative.
- Sources say the Allenby bridge between Jordan and the West Bank is still closed to Palestinians trying to get to West Bank towns of Jericho and Nablus.

- Hamas's Moussa Abu Marzouq says his recent meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat did not contradict Hamas policy. Says Hamas welcomes any meeting which serves the purpose of the Palestinian people.
- Sources say Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour given responsibility for dialogue with opposition parties over whether they will take part in elections.
- Only tourists and Jerusalem residents allowed across border between Jordan and West Bank.
- Lawyers' association calls for new court fees to be cancelled after increases of between 66 pct to 200 pct.
- Head of Moslem Brotherhood says there's no mediation between government and opposition over election boycott.
- Ministers to hold emergency meeting at Interior Ministry today to discuss elections.
- Cabinet briefed on new visa measures at border posts.
- Crown Prince Hassan reiterates importance of containing crisis facing peace talks.
